label: q fed back as input during copy phase of short sequences (L<=5)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (t > L), and essentially only when the input token is q (99.4% of activation mass), i.e. right after the model has output q and it is fed back in. Never fires in the original or delimiter phases, and not on q in the original sequence. Strongly gated by sequence length: L=3-4 has the highest rate (precision 0.96 for q-input at L<=4), L=5 is partial, and L>=6 rarely fires (weak activations). Largest activations come from very short sequences where q is early in the copy (recall_idx 1-2, right after <DEL>), especially with repeated q (q q x). Within L=5 activation depends on position and digit count in ways not fully captured. Predicate (copy phase, q input, L<=5): dev F1 0.75, mass recall 0.93; the plain q-in-copy-phase predicate gets mass recall 0.99 but precision only 0.18 because of long sequences.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: q, w, c, a, l, d; least: 2, h, j, m) and the token being output (most: q, c, w, 3, l, a; least: j, i, m, -); timing cues that raise it most: L=3, t=5, L=3 & t=5.
